nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Extreme weather events|Coastal and inland flooding_qna_000
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why is sea-level rise included in the assessments of future risk for areas likely to be permanently flooded?
nodes.answer: Sea-level rise is considered a long-term risk that could affect large areas that are expected to be permanently flooded in the coming decades and centuries.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Background Large quantities of persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and other persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic sub - stances (PBTs) like heavy metals have accumulated mainly over the last century in reservoirs, such as landfills, dump sites, contaminated sites, and mine tailings, as well as in environmental sinks like soils and sediments. Large floods in the past 20 years have demonstrated the mobilisation of POPs/PBTs from these reservoirs, underscoring the limitations of conven- tional technical safeguard measures like leachate and wastewater treatment or containment systems at landfills. Results This study emphasises the need to develop inventories of POPs/PBTs in these reservoirs for the assessment of future risk of increased flooding triggered by climate change and for priority setting of remediation and securing measures. Further, sea-level rise should be included in these assessments as long-term risk for large areas that are likely to be permanently flooded in the coming decades and centuries. In addition, the risk of release of POPs and other PBTs by industries affected by Natural Hazards Triggering Technological Accidents (Natech) should be globally evaluated. The review emphasises the importance of conducting systematic assessments and inventories to understand the risk of these reservoirs for environmental pollution and human exposure.

nodes.answer: Floods destroyed over 676,000 hectares of farmland in 2022.

nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: Why are coastal regions particularly vulnerable to climate-induced sea-level rise?
nodes.answer: Coastal regions are increasingly vulnerable due to increased flood risks associated with sea-level rise.
nodes.paragraph: A lack of familiarity with coastal climate adaptation strategies among marginalized and vulnerable populations can lead to insufficient support for these strategies aimed at mitigating climate risks, exacerbating the issue of climate justice. Keywords Coastal management Climate justice Climate adaptation Socio- demographic disparity 3 Natural Hazards (2025) 121:3603 36191 Introduction Global sea levels have risen considerably in the 20th century and sea-level rise (SLR) is projected to accelerate through the 21st century and beyond (Nicholls and Cazenave 2010 ). With climate-induced SLR continuing to affect human activities adversely, coastal regions are particularly vulnerable due to increased flood risks (Wing et al. 2022 ). To mitigate the negative consequences of SLR in coastal regions, various adaptation measures for infra - structure through different adaptation strategies have been increasingly implemented worldwide. To economically justify these adaptation measures which are often funded by government agencies, a growing number of studies have explored households willingness to pay (WTP) for different coastal climate adaptation strategies (see Johnston et al. 2018 ; Ardeshiri et al. 2019 ; Landry et al. 2020 ; Meyerhoff et al.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which three counties are highlighted as ideal case studies for climate adaptation measures due to their vulnerability to flooding and sea level rise?
nodes.answer: The three counties are Broward County, Miami-Dade County, and Palm Beach County.
nodes.paragraph: These three counties provide an ideal and compelling case study given the frequent flood - ing from Hurricanes and tropical storms (e.g., Hurricane Andrew in 1992 and Hurricane Irma in 2017), the large population at low elevations, increasing threats from SLR, and the growing need for climate adaptation measures for infrastructure. Coastal areas in the study region are especially vulnerable to SLR as it is projected that the sea level will rise about 6 to 10 inches by 2030 and 14 to 26 inches by 2060. In the long term, SLR is projected to be 31 to 61 inches by 2100 (Sea Level Rise Work Group 2015 ). Considering that the average elevation of Broward County, Miami-Dade County, and Palm Beach County is 72, 72, and 84 inches, respectively, the continued SLR will pose an existential threat to the region if no adaptation measures are to be implemented. 1 See the 2020 Census data for Broward County ( https://data.census.gov/all? q =Broward%20County,%20 Florida ), Miami-Dade County ( https://data.census.gov/all? q =Miami-Dade%20County,%20Florida ), and Palm Beach County ( https://data.census.gov/all?

nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What aspect did UNEP emphasize in relation to flooding and POPs?
nodes.answer: UNEP stressed the relevance of flooding and the risk of release of POPs and other chemicals of concern.
nodes.paragraph: However, e.g., for PCDD/PCDF, PCBs or hexachlorocyclohexane (HCH) isomers, the reservoirs in soils and sediments are a main determining factor for today S exposure or exposure risk USEPA [198, 212, 348, 351, 361, 332]. Because of their high persistence, these compounds will not degrade in these reservoirs for extended time frames probably for centuries and longer [361, 362]. Over these extended timescales, consideration needs to be given to the impacts of climate change in the next decades and centuries. A range of interlinks have been described between climate change and POPs in a review for the UN [322]. In the latter publication and in a review [207], the focus is rather on global flows and emphasises, e.g., the relevance of temperature on vola tility or the impact on the Arctic and does not highlight flooding and remobilisation from landfills and other reservoirs [207, 322]. However, in a recent publica tion on chemicals, wastes, and climate change, UNEP stressed the relevance of flooding and the risk of release of POPs and other chemicals of concern [314].
